prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the very near interior surfaces and partial person at the image edges (roughly 0.2–0.8 m) from the seats and dashboard (about 0.7–1.5 m) and the exterior house/garage (roughly 3–8 m). Across frames 1–3, a close person or body region shifts from the left edge to the right side and remains partly out of view, while the seats stay behind it; frames 4–5 turn forward, placing the steering wheel and dashboard below/in front and the garage farther ahead. It makes near–far ordering and occlusion boundaries clearer than RGB, including which interior objects are plausibly within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach. Absolute metre estimates are unreliable because the map is monocular, and several boundaries—especially windows, the steering wheel, bright body regions, and the exterior person in frame 5—appear smoothed or assigned inconsistent depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map marks partial people at the extreme left of frame 1, extreme right of frame 3, and near the center-right of frame 5; the first two appear within about 0.2–0.8 m of the camera, whereas the final person outside is several metres ahead. It also isolates overlapping regions near the middle-right of frame 2 and a large foreground/interior region in frame 4, making occlusion and coarse left/right occupancy easier to see than in RGB. The masks show the close people cut off by the frame boundaries and indicate that the frame-2 objects overlap spatially, but they do not reliably establish facing direction, gaze, above/below relations, or inter-object distance. The class labels are visibly unreliable: seat/interior regions are labelled “banana,” and much of the car/exterior region is labelled “motorcycle,” while many clear RGB objects—including seats, steering wheel, car structure, house, and garage—are missing.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it detects no body or hand skeletons and provides no usable joint positions, facing direction, gaze direction, reach envelope, or person-to-object geometry. Consequently, it cannot show the close partial person moving from the left edge in frame 1 to the right side by frame 3, nor the more distant person ahead in frame 5. It adds no spatial information beyond the RGB and cannot confirm whether any hand or object is within someone’s arm’s reach. Its failure is plausibly related to severe cropping, occlusion, unusual egocentric viewpoints, and small or partly visible bodies, but the map itself only establishes that pose estimation was unsuccessful.
